header: Whether what a live card shows is live, the last close, or a saved copy: I decide it in one place so that every card says it in the same three words and the same three colours: "live" - green: a figure from the session that is running now (a share price at most 20 minutes old inside market hours; today's IBJA rate once IBJA has put it up) "last" - grey: the last figure the source published, which is the right answer now (a market that is shut; IBJA on a Sunday, a holiday, or before its morning rate) "saved" - amber: the source did not answer, and this is the last copy this site kept, with its own time I need no calendar for a holiday: on a day the exchange is shut the newest price is the old close, more than 20 minutes old, so it reads "last".

symbols.name: goldFreshness
symbols.sig: export function goldFreshness(r: { asOf?: string; session: "AM" | "PM" }, stale: boolean): FreshnessLabel
doc: I mark the IBJA gold and silver rates as saved when only a saved copy could be had, as today's rate once it is up, and otherwise as the last day IBJA published.

behaviours: a price a few minutes old, inside the session, is LIVE
the same price, 25 minutes old, is the last close (the feed has stopped or the day is a holiday)
before the opening bell, yesterday's close is the LAST CLOSE
after the close, the day's last price is the LAST CLOSE
on a Sunday the last price is the LAST CLOSE, however fresh the fetch
a weekday market holiday needs no calendar: the newest price is the old close, so it reads LAST CLOSE
a price at 9:20, five minutes after the bell, is LIVE
a saved copy is SAVED COPY even when its time is recent; another name beside it is not
a time that cannot be read is never called live
gold: today's rate with no asOf is live: the opening (AM) rate, then the closing (PM) rate
gold: when IBJA has put up nothing for today, the pill is the last published day, in grey
gold: a saved copy is SAVED COPY whatever else is true
every label carries a sentence for the tooltip and the screen reader
